qualitative.note: Fails Gate 1 (Reject – G1 Understandability). Outside the one-off COVID-19 pandemic windfall (2021–2022), Moderna lacks an established, multi-cycle profitable commercial economic engine. Revenue collapsed by ~90% from a $19.3B peak in FY22 to $1.94B in FY25, generating cumulative net losses exceeding $11B across FY23–FY25 alongside continuous multi-billion cash burn. Its ongoing intrinsic valuation hinges on speculative, binary clinical trial readouts and regulatory clearances across an unproven developmental pipeline, placing it outside the Munger circle of competence.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial collapse following the pandemic demand cliff: Revenues plummeted from $18.47B (FY21) and $19.26B (FY22) to $6.85B (FY23), $3.20B (FY24), and $1.94B (FY25). GAAP net losses totaled $(4.71B) in FY23, $(3.56B) in FY24, and $(2.82B) in FY25, with free cash flow of $(4.06B) in FY24 and $(2.07B) in FY25. Despite a seasonal Q3 2026 profit of $162M, full-year operations remain heavily loss-making. To support ongoing R&D cash burn, Moderna issued $2.6B in convertible debt in late 2026. Commercial products are currently limited to Spikevax and mRESVIA in saturated respiratory vaccine markets. The platform has not demonstrated self-sustaining commercial profitability outside government emergency pandemic procurement.
